newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

SUGAR: World market for September 10 - White sugar futures in London closed mixed with October up $0.90 at $349.00. In New York raw sugar futures ended unchanged to slightly higher with October up 2 points at 12.05 cents/lb while March remained unchanged at 11.73 cents/lb. The back months closed 2 to 9 points higher.

Speculators continued to role out of the October contract ahead of its September 30 expiry. Traders also expect the October contract to continue to hover near the 12.00 cents strike price ahead of the option's expiry, with near 20,000 lots of October calls still in the money up to 12.00 cents/lb. The October/March switch ended at 0.32 cent compared to 0.30 cent on Monday. Given prospects of another surplus in 1996/97, no major rally seems in sight.

EUROPE - The eastern part of western Europe received adequate rains during the period ended September 10, while the western areas were mostly dry. Farmers said the moisture could become detrimental for the crop in the east.

In the former Soviet Union, sugar beet areas received widespread rains. The moisture was generally sufficient to end stress but hampered early harvest activity. If the rains should continue this could become a problem especially in Russia, where the sector usually suffers from a lack of harvesting machinery and insufficient transport capacities.

FRANCE - France exported 193,440 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in June 1996, 33 per cent less than was exported the same month the previous year. That brought total exports since the beginning of 1995/96 (October) up to 2.3 million tonnes, down from 2.5 million tonnes exported the same period in 1994/95. Total exports in crop year 1994/95 (October/September) reached 3.1 million tonnes, up from 2.8 million tonnes in 1993/94.
Major export markets for white sugar in October/June 1995/96 were Turkey (170,267 vs 28,928 tonnes), Iran (158,800 vs 168,013 tonnes) and Syria (151,131 vs 33,046 tonnes).

The country imported 375,952 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in October/June 1995/96, sharply up on last year's figure of 255,762 tonnes. Total imports in crop year 1994/95 reached 364,140 tonnes down from 389,982 tonnes the previous year. Sugar consumption in October/June 1995/96 reached 1.582 million tonnes, down 0.8 per cent on last year.

INDIA - India exported 840,196 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in October/August 1995/96, which compares to 30,929 tonnes exported the same period in 1994/95. Total exports in crop year 1994/95 (October/September) reached 37,722 tonnes up from 28,013 tonnes exported in 1993/94. Major export markets for Indian white sugar in October/August 1995/96 were Russia (90,000 tonnes), Indonesia (205,810 tonnes), Pakistan (144,216 tonnes) and Sri Lanka (173,765 tonnes).
India sold 12 cargoes of 60 and 100 ICUMSA sugar for October through March shipment, trade sources said. It was added that the country was also considering the sale of another 12 cargoes.
